text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Centre-right Diko and right-wing Disy parties agree to cooperate in December's municipal elections.
- President's daughter said "she would not rule out" loving a Turkish Cypriot.
- Cyprus Airways hopes to break even by the end of the year.
CYPRUS MAIL
- UNFICYP peacekeeping force raps Greek Cypriot protests at the Ledra Palace discouraging tourists from visiting the north.
- Debate whether to fly the Greek flag or not at Cyprus university divides students.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Cyprus Airways reports a massive loss.
- Foreign investors who made bids to participate in Bank of Cyprus convertible bond issue are confident there is scope for more gains after deregulation, says bank chairman Solon Triantafyllides.
HARAVGHI
- The government minces its words now over President Glafcos Clerides's statements that political parties are not his guardians. Government officials make "clarifications" to tone down reactions.
- Company likely to get contract to build a power station in Vassiliko built one in occupied Kyrenia.
PHILELEPHTHEROS

- A flurry of diplomatic activity starts on the Cyprus problem in mid-November to prepare the ground for possible negotiations between President Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash in 1997.
- Education ministry survey says 4.4 percent of students have taken drugs.
- Cyprus Chamber of Commerce and Industry calls for privatisations and legislation to control strikes.
SIMERINI
- Students of Cyprus's university say they will shut it if the Greek flag is lowered.
- Significant decisions will be taken concerning the future of Cyprus Airways at the next cabinet meeting.
